text:
The Fed didn't cut rates to zero in 2024. It cut three times, in September (50 bp), November (25 bp), and December (25 bp), taking the federal funds target from 5.25-5.50% to 4.25-4.50%. The reason was that inflation had fallen enough toward 2% and the labor market was cooling, so it began easing from a restrictive level.

You may be thinking of the near-zero rate periods: December 2008 through 2015, and March 2020, when the Fed cut to 0-0.25% in response to the COVID-19 shock.
